A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Scaling Laws For Scalable Oversight, with the same framework, oversight games, and NSO analysis. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM experiments on Counting-to-21 and four oversight games, including pairwise win rates, fitted Elo ratings, backdoor diagnostics, and Wargames strategy analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original game experiments and appendix analyses, alongside revised fitted Elo results and numerical NSO predictions.

M1.justification: The role-specific Elo estimation, Double-ReLU model, AIC fit selection, and equally spaced NSO objective remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 document existing game procedures rather than introduce new components. The sigmoid alternative is discussed but not implemented or evaluated.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Counting-to-21, Mafia, Debate on TruthfulQA, BoolQ, QuaLITY, and PrOntoQA, Backdoor Code on competition-level APPS problems, and the same Wargames scenario. Moving additional results into different appendices does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same 14 models, with Gemini-Pro excluded from Debate and Claude-3.5-Haiku excluded from Wargames in both versions. The NSO comparison against single-step oversight also remains. V3's discussion of random judging does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V1 Section 4.1 describes searching n = 1–20 and then larger n until success probability decreases; v3 specifies only n = 1–20. The illustrative NSO configurations also change between v1 Figure 9 and v3 Figure 6. Empirical sample counts and game budgets remain unchanged; these reporting revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 removes the explicit R² goodness-of-fit assessment accompanying Figure 3 and shortens the Wargames case study by omitting its first-month plans and updates. The backdoor viability and conditional-success analyses, Wargames strategy profiles and prompt-hardening observations, and NSO slope-sensitivity study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify statistical bootstrapping with 200 random seeds for Elo confidence intervals and retain Table 1's Arena 95% confidence intervals. Although plotted interval values change, neither version documents a different uncertainty-estimation procedure or an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Several fitted Elo points, curves, and interval values change in Figures 2–3 and the additional Debate plots, while the pairwise win-rate heatmaps remain unchanged. Section 4.4 revises the 400-point-gap NSO estimates from 9.8% to 9.4% for Wargames and 51.4% to 51.7% for Debate. These are revised model-based predictions, not demonstrated performance gains. Figure 3's eight R² values are removed.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the long-term risk equations: v1's negative exponent in the control-survival probability becomes t/τ, and the half-life denominator becomes log[1−pc(ASI)] rather than [1−pc(ASI)]. These are mathematical corrections, not notation changes. The core NSO derivations and asymptotic proofs are retained, largely relocated to Appendix G.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain the Double-ReLU scaling framework, its application to four oversight games, and theoretical optimization of NSO. The abstract replaces the below-52% summary with game-specific estimates but retains the same low-success conclusion at a 400-point capability gap.

C2.justification: V3 explains that domain Elo is game-specific and motivates Double-ReLU over alternatives such as a sigmoid. Section 4.4 adds Debate's 50% chance baseline and assumptions connecting auditing, knowledge elicitation, and containment to NSO. Conversely, v1's explicit qualification that equally spaced protocols provide only a lower bound on achievable success is omitted, although the spacing assumption remains in the equations.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds four game-evaluation pseudocode algorithms. The prompts and most experimental details are retained or relocated. V3 omits v1's February 20, 2025 Arena-score snapshot date and its disclosure of clipping negative fitted slopes to zero for NSO calculations; these are documentation losses, not evidence that those procedures changed.

R1.justification: V3 adds Singh et al.'s The Leaderboard Illusion and model-source citations in Table 1, while removing references including Chiang et al., CodeElo, CodeJudge, and some risk-motivation sources. The substantive related-work discussion and central research positioning remain largely unchanged, moving from Section 5 to Appendix B.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and condensed. Game details, formal definitions, fitting details, related work, and proofs move into reorganized appendices; contributions are consolidated, and the conclusion is shortened with explicit recommendations. This substantially changes the narrative structure beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: Several main-text figures move into appendices. The Wargames transcript is substantially shortened, the NSO schematic and examples are arranged side by side, and four example panels become two. The R² table is removed, Table 1 gains a citation column, and four algorithm displays are added. Together these substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 fixes genuine errors in the risk-decay and half-life equations and improves interpretation through Debate's chance baseline and explicit NSO applicability assumptions. The reorganized exposition and pseudocode also aid understanding. These limited gains are partly offset by removing the R² diagnostics and the explicit lower-bound caveat for equally spaced oversight; the empirical foundation remains largely unchanged.
